cultivar: AV2 (Ambari Vegetative 2), a clone prized for sweet, floral leaf and large downy buds
processing: Very lightly oxidised first-flush processing of clonal AV2 leaf: a long wither, the gentlest rolling and minimal oxidation before a careful low-temperature dry, giving a leaf that stays mostly green and silver and a cup close to white tea.
harvest_season: Spring, the earliest first-flush pickings from March to early April.
appearance_dry: Large, loosely twisted leaf in pale green and silver with abundant white downy tips.
appearance_wet: Whole, pale green leaves and buds.
taste_profile: Intensely aromatic: white flowers, lychee, green grape and a honeyed sweetness over a soft texture with only a light grip at the end.

brewing.notes: Cool water and a short first steep; hot water or a long steep wastes the aroma you paid for. Expect two or three good infusions.

vintage_note: Sold as a named first-flush lot ('Moonlight', 'Clonal Special', 'AV2 Supreme', 'Clonal Delight') with the garden, the invoice number and the harvest year; among the most expensive Darjeelings, shipping from late March in small quantities and often by pre-order. Drink within the year of harvest: the aroma that justifies the price is the first thing to go.
description:
'Moonlight' is the name several Darjeeling estates give to their lightest, most aromatic first-flush lots, almost always made from the AV2 clonal bush: large, pale, silvery leaf, barely oxidised, with a cup that sits somewhere between a white tea and a first flush. Castleton's is the best known, several other gardens sell one, and these lots usually top the garden's spring price list.

AV2 (Ambari Vegetative 2) is a clone selected decades ago for its sweet, floral leaf and big, downy buds, and it has become the signature bush of modern high-end Darjeeling. For a Moonlight lot the earliest spring pickings are given a very long wither, the gentlest rolling and the shortest possible oxidation before a careful low-temperature dry, so the leaf stays pale, silvery and whole.

The aroma is the point: white flowers, lychee, green grape and a honeyed sweetness over a soft, round texture with only a light grip at the end. Brew it cool, around 85 °C, for three minutes, and expect two or three good steeps; hot water or a long first steep wastes everything that makes it expensive.

It is sold as a named first-flush lot ('Moonlight', 'Clonal Special', 'AV2 Supreme') with the garden, the invoice number and the year, and it ships from late March in small quantities, often by pre-order. Because 'Moonlight' is a marketing name rather than a grade, two gardens' versions can differ a lot; buy from a seller who names the invoice.

Drink it within the year of harvest. The aroma that justifies the price is the first thing to fade, so this is not a tea to save for a special occasion a year away.
sources_note: 'Moonlight' is a marketing name used by several estates (Castleton, Jungpana, Goomtee, Margaret's Hope) for very light AV2 first-flush lots, not a defined grade; category set to black because it is sold as a first-flush black tea even though it is barely oxidised.
